q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Works expenditure is classified under Major Heads 5002 and 5003 by Plan Heads, irrespective of the fund from which a work is financed.
2. Revenue working expenses are classified under Major Head 3002 by Sub-Major Heads and Primary Units, and not by Plan Heads.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Works expenditure under Major Heads 5002 and 5003 is classified by Plan Heads irrespective of the financing fund, while revenue working expenses under Major Head 3002 are classified by Sub-Major Heads and Primary Units.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'debt heads' from 'remittance heads' of account?

options.A: Debt heads record amounts in the course of remittance between officers, whereas remittance heads record definite liabilities of the Railways
options.B: Both debt heads and remittance heads record only the earnings of the Railways awaiting apportionment
options.C: Debt heads record transactions representing definite liabilities of, or amounts recoverable by, the Railways, such as deposits and provident fund balances, whereas remittance heads record amounts in the course of remittance between officers and banks, pending credit or settlement
options.D: Debt heads are operated only in the books of the Railway Board, whereas remittance heads are operated only at stations

e: Debt heads record definite liabilities of, or amounts recoverable by, the Railways, such as deposits and provident fund. Remittance heads record amounts in transit between officers and banks pending credit or settlement.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the annual compilation of the commercial accounts of a railway after the March (Final) accounts are closed?

options.A: Preparation of the Balance Sheet — closing entries in the General Books — extraction of the Trial Balance — preparation of the Capital Account and the Revenue Account
options.B: Extraction of the Trial Balance — preparation of the Balance Sheet — closing entries in the General Books — preparation of the Capital Account and the Revenue Account
options.C: Preparation of the Capital Account and the Revenue Account — extraction of the Trial Balance — closing entries in the General Books — preparation of the Balance Sheet
options.D: Closing entries in the General Books — extraction of the Trial Balance — preparation of the Capital Account, the Revenue Account and the Balance Sheet from the closed books

e: After March Final accounts, closing entries are passed in the General Books, the Trial Balance is extracted, and the Capital Account, Revenue Account and Balance Sheet are then prepared from the closed books.

q: An existing station building, which has become dilapidated, is replaced by a new building of the same size and capacity on the same site, without any material enhancement of capacity. The cost of the replacement is chargeable to:

options.A: The Depreciation Reserve Fund, the work being a renewal and replacement of an existing asset
options.B: Capital in all cases, a new building having been constructed
options.C: The ordinary working expenses of the year as a repair
options.D: The Development Fund in all cases

e: Replacement of a dilapidated station building by one of the same size and capacity, without material enhancement, is a renewal and replacement. Its cost is chargeable to the Depreciation Reserve Fund.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'surrender' of funds from the 'lapse' of a grant?

options.A: Surrender is the automatic extinction of a grant at the close of the year, whereas lapse is the return of savings during the year
options.B: Surrender is the return, during the course of the year, of savings anticipated under a grant to the controlling authority, whereas lapse is the automatic extinction of the unspent balance of a grant at the close of the financial year
options.C: Both surrender and lapse take place only at the close of the financial year
options.D: Surrender requires a vote of Parliament, whereas lapse is ordered by the controlling authority

e: Surrender is the return during the year of anticipated savings to the controlling authority. Lapse is the automatic extinction of the unspent balance of a grant at the close of the financial year.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Funds surrendered by a unit out of a grant revert to the controlling authority and may be re-allotted by it to other units or heads within the same grant.
2. Savings surrendered under one grant may be utilised by the controlling authority to meet excess expenditure under another grant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct. Surrendered funds may be re-allotted within the same grant, but savings under one grant cannot be used to meet excess under another grant.

q:
Consider the following statements about errors and the Trial Balance:
1. An error of principle, such as booking a capital item of expenditure as a revenue item, does not disturb the agreement of the Trial Balance, the amounts debited and credited being unaffected.
2. The agreement of the Trial Balance proves that no error of principle has been committed in the books.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: Neither 1 nor 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: 1 only

e: Only statement 1 is correct. An error of principle does not affect debit and credit totals, so the Trial Balance still agrees; its agreement therefore does not prove that no error of principle exists.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a Journal Voucher from a cash voucher in the railway accounts?

options.A: A Journal Voucher supports a transfer (adjustment) entry in the Journal Book, whereas a cash voucher supports a receipt or payment made through the Cash & Pay Office
options.B: A Journal Voucher supports payments made by the Cash & Pay Office, whereas a cash voucher supports adjustment entries in the Journal Book
options.C: Both the vouchers support only the earnings transactions of stations
options.D: A Journal Voucher is prepared by the Audit Department, whereas a cash voucher is prepared by the Railway Board

e: A Journal Voucher supports a transfer or adjustment entry in the Journal Book. A cash voucher supports a receipt or payment made through the Cash and Pay Office.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Main Cash Book and the Journal Book are subsidiary books of a railway, in which transactions are first recorded in detail.
2. The Ledger is a General Book, in which the transactions are posted in classified form under the heads of account.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: 2 only

e: Both statements are correct. The Main Cash Book and Journal Book are subsidiary books where transactions are first recorded in detail, while the Ledger is a General Book where they are posted in classified form.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Vote on Account' from a 'token grant'?

options.A: A Vote on Account is a nominal grant for a new service, whereas a token grant is a grant in advance for a part of the financial year
options.B: Both a Vote on Account and a token grant are grants in advance for a part of the financial year
options.C: A Vote on Account is a grant in advance for a part of the financial year, pending the completion of the budgetary process for the year, whereas a token grant is a nominal grant taken for a new service whose cost can be met by re-appropriation within the grant
options.D: A Vote on Account is voted by the Rajya Sabha, whereas a token grant is voted by the Lok Sabha

e: A Vote on Account is a grant in advance for part of the year pending completion of the budget process. A token grant is a nominal grant for a new service whose cost is met by re-appropriation within the grant.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Extra Budgetary Resources through Institutional Finance, mobilised through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation, are used mainly for the acquisition of rolling stock.
2. Of the lease charges payable to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation, the capital component is charged under the Plan Head for leased assets and the interest component is charged to the revenue working expenses.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Neither 1 nor 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are correct. IRFC institutional finance is used mainly for rolling stock acquisition, and lease charges are split: the capital component under the Plan Head for leased assets and the interest component to revenue working expenses.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Gross Budgetary Support from the internal resources of the Railways?

options.A: Gross Budgetary Support is the support extended to the Railways through the Union Budget out of the general revenues of the Government, whereas the internal resources of the Railways are generated by the Railways themselves and include their surplus (net revenue) and the amounts appropriated to the Railway Funds
options.B: Gross Budgetary Support is generated by the Railways out of their surplus, whereas internal resources are provided through the Union Budget
options.C: Market borrowings raised through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation are a part of Gross Budgetary Support
options.D: Both Gross Budgetary Support and internal resources are raised from the market by the Railways

e: Gross Budgetary Support is provided through the Union Budget from general revenues. Internal resources are generated by the Railways themselves and include surplus and appropriations to Railway Funds.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an advance from the Contingency Fund of India from a Supplementary Grant?

options.A: An advance from the Contingency Fund of India is itself the authorisation of Parliament for additional expenditure, whereas a supplementary grant is recouped to the Fund after authorisation
options.B: An advance from the Contingency Fund of India is taken to meet urgent unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament and is recouped after the authorisation, whereas a supplementary grant is itself the authorisation obtained from Parliament during the year for additional expenditure or a new service
options.C: Both an advance from the Contingency Fund and a supplementary grant are voted by the Rajya Sabha
options.D: An advance from the Contingency Fund of India requires no recoupment in any case, whereas a supplementary grant is always recouped

e: A Contingency Fund advance meets urgent unforeseen expenditure pending Parliament authorisation and is recouped after authorisation. A supplementary grant is itself the authorisation obtained from Parliament during the year.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Demands Recoverable' from 'Miscellaneous Advances' in the railway accounts?

options.A: 'Demands Recoverable' represents advances made by the Railways for purchases, whereas 'Miscellaneous Advances' represents amounts due for services rendered
options.B: Both the heads represent amounts held by the Railways on behalf of outside parties, pending payment to them
options.C: 'Demands Recoverable' represents amounts due to the Railways from outside parties for goods supplied or services rendered, pending realisation, whereas 'Miscellaneous Advances' represents advances made by the Railways which are recoverable or adjustable in due course
options.D: 'Demands Recoverable' is a remittance head, whereas 'Miscellaneous Advances' is a head of the earnings accounts

e: Demands Recoverable are amounts due from outside parties for goods supplied or services rendered, pending realisation. Miscellaneous Advances are advances made by the Railways, recoverable or adjustable in due course.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Preliminary Works Programme from the Pink Book?

options.A: The Preliminary Works Programme is the programme as finally approved by the Railway Board, whereas the Pink Book contains the proposals submitted by the zonal railways
options.B: Both the Preliminary Works Programme and the Pink Book contain only works which have already been sanctioned
options.C: The Preliminary Works Programme lists the approved works Plan Head-wise, whereas the Pink Book records the expenditure incurred on each work
options.D: The Preliminary Works Programme contains the proposals submitted by a zonal railway for works to be included in the following year's programme, whereas the Pink Book is the Works Programme as finally approved, listing the approved works Plan Head-wise with the provision made for them

e: The Preliminary Works Programme contains a zonal railway proposals for the following year programme. The Pink Book is the Works Programme as finally approved, listing approved works Plan Head-wise with provision.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an Interim Budget from a regular (full) Budget?

options.A: An Interim Budget is presented in an election year by the outgoing Government and, with a Vote on Account, provides mainly for the initial part of the year pending the presentation of the regular Budget by the new Government, whereas a regular Budget presents the Annual Financial Statement and the Demands for Grants for the whole financial year
options.B: An Interim Budget is presented by the new Government after the elections, whereas a regular Budget is presented by the outgoing Government
options.C: An Interim Budget presents the Demands for Grants for the whole financial year and is passed like a regular Budget in all respects
options.D: An Interim Budget is presented only to the Rajya Sabha, whereas a regular Budget is presented only to the Lok Sabha

e: An Interim Budget is presented in an election year by the outgoing Government and, with a Vote on Account, covers mainly the initial part of the year. A regular Budget covers the whole financial year.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. After the merger of the Railway Budget with the Union Budget, the expenditure of the Railways is provided for through a single Demand for Grants of the Ministry of Railways within the Union Budget.
2. Notwithstanding the merger, the accounts of the Railways continue to be compiled by the Railways through their own accounts organisation, and were not taken over by the Controller General of Accounts.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. After merger, railway expenditure is provided through a single Demand for Grants of the Ministry of Railways, yet railway accounts continue to be compiled by the Railways own organisation, not the Controller General of Accounts.

q:
Consider the following statements about a new railway line under construction:
1. The net earnings, if any, of the line before it is opened for public traffic are credited to the Capital account of the work, in reduction of its cost.
2. After the line is opened for public traffic, its earnings are taken to the revenue earnings of the Railways and its working expenses are charged to revenue.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: Neither 1 nor 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: 2 only

e: Both statements are correct. Net earnings of a line before opening for public traffic are credited to its Capital account in reduction of cost; after opening, earnings go to revenue and working expenses are charged to revenue.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The balance under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' in the books of a zonal railway is reconciled periodically with the statement of the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank of India.
2. Differences brought out by the reconciliation are adjusted in the railway books through the head 'Reserve Bank Suspense'.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are correct. Deposits with Reserve Bank is reconciled with the Reserve Bank Central Accounts Section statement, and differences are adjusted through Reserve Bank Suspense.

q: A workshop of one zonal railway manufactures components and supplies them to another zonal railway for use on that railway. The cost of the components supplied is adjusted between the two railways:

options.A: Through transfer transactions, the cost being credited to the Manufacturing Suspense of the manufacturing railway and debited to the receiving railway
options.B: By daily remittance of cash by the receiving railway to the manufacturing railway
options.C: By crediting the cost to the Sundry Other Earnings of the manufacturing railway
options.D: By debiting the cost to the Contingency Fund of India through the Railway Board

e: Inter-railway supply of workshop manufactures is settled by transfer transactions. The cost is credited to Manufacturing Suspense of the manufacturing railway and debited to the receiving railway, with no cash remittance.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes DF-I from DF-II of the Development Fund of the Railways?

options.A: DF-I finances labour welfare works, whereas DF-II finances works of passenger and other railway user amenities
options.B: DF-I finances works of passenger and other railway user amenities, whereas DF-II finances labour welfare works
options.C: Both DF-I and DF-II finance unremunerative operational improvement works
options.D: DF-I and DF-II are subdivisions of the Capital Fund, and not of the Development Fund

e: Development Fund subdivision DF-I finances passenger and other railway user amenities works, while DF-II finances labour welfare works.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the preparation and examination of the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways after the accounts of the year are closed?

options.A: Examination by the Public Accounts Committee — comparison of actual expenditure with the Final Grant — audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General — recording of explanations of variations
options.B: Audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General — laying before Parliament — comparison of actual expenditure with the Final Grant — recording of explanations of variations
options.C: Recording of explanations of variations — laying before Parliament — audit by the Comptroller and Auditor General — comparison of actual expenditure with the Final Grant
options.D: Comparison of actual expenditure with the Final Grant and the Final Appropriation — recording of explanations of variations — audit on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General — laying before Parliament with the Audit Report — examination by the Public Accounts Committee

e: Appropriation Accounts are prepared by comparing actuals with the Final Grant and Final Appropriation and recording variation explanations, audited for the CAG, laid before Parliament with the Audit Report, and examined by the Public Accounts Committee.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the authorisation and distribution of a grant after the Demands for Grants have been voted by the Lok Sabha?

options.A: Appropriation Bill passed by Parliament — assent of the President — Appropriation Act — communication of the budget allotment by the Railway Board — distribution of the allotment among the divisions and units by the zonal headquarters
options.B: Assent of the President — Appropriation Bill passed by Parliament — distribution of the allotment among the divisions — Appropriation Act — communication of the allotment by the Railway Board
options.C: Communication of the budget allotment by the Railway Board — Appropriation Act — assent of the President — Appropriation Bill passed by Parliament — distribution of the allotment among the divisions
options.D: Appropriation Act — communication of the budget allotment by the Railway Board — Appropriation Bill passed by Parliament — assent of the President — distribution of the allotment among the divisions

e: After Demands are voted, the Appropriation Bill is passed, the President assents and the Appropriation Act results; the Railway Board then communicates allotments and zonal headquarters distributes them to divisions and units.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the clearance of an item booked under a suspense head of account?

options.A: Adjustment to the final head of account — booking under the suspense head — entry in the Suspense Register — periodic review of the outstanding item
options.B: Entry in the Suspense Register — adjustment to the final head of account — booking under the suspense head — periodic review of the outstanding item
options.C: Periodic review of the outstanding item — booking under the suspense head — adjustment to the final head of account — entry in the Suspense Register
options.D: Booking under the suspense head — entry of the item in the Suspense Register — periodic review and pursuit of the item with the unit or party concerned — adjustment to the final head of account through a transfer entry

e: A suspense item is first booked under the suspense head, entered in the Suspense Register, periodically reviewed and pursued with the unit or party concerned, and finally adjusted to the final head by transfer entry.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a Money Bill from an ordinary Bill in relation to the powers of the President?

options.A: The President can return both a Money Bill and an ordinary Bill to Parliament for reconsideration
options.B: The President cannot return a Money Bill for the reconsideration of Parliament, whereas an ordinary Bill, which is not a Money Bill, can be returned by the President for reconsideration
options.C: The President can return a Money Bill for reconsideration, whereas an ordinary Bill cannot be returned at all
options.D: Neither a Money Bill nor an ordinary Bill requires the assent of the President

e: Under Article 111 the President may return an ordinary Bill for reconsideration but cannot return a Money Bill. A Money Bill can only be assented to or withheld.

q: A Money Bill passed by the Lok Sabha is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha, which does not return it to the Lok Sabha within fourteen days of its receipt. The position is that:

options.A: The Bill is deemed to have been passed by both Houses of Parliament in the form in which it was passed by the Lok Sabha
options.B: The Bill is deemed to have been rejected by Parliament
options.C: The Bill is returned to the Lok Sabha for being passed afresh
options.D: The Bill can become law only after a joint sitting of both Houses is held

e: Under Article 109, if the Rajya Sabha does not return a Money Bill within fourteen days, it is deemed passed by both Houses in the form passed by the Lok Sabha.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. If any question arises whether a Bill is a Money Bill or not, the decision of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha thereon is final.
2. When a Money Bill is transmitted to the Rajya Sabha, there is endorsed on it the certificate of the Speaker of the Lok Sabha that it is a Money Bill.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Under Article 110 the Speaker decision on whether a Bill is a Money Bill is final, and the Speaker certificate to that effect is endorsed on the Bill when transmitted to the Rajya Sabha.

q: The amount granted by the Lok Sabha through a Vote on Account for the initial part of a financial year is:

options.A: An amount sanctioned in addition to the grant for the whole year, which is voted separately over and above it
options.B: A charge on the Contingency Fund of India, which is not adjusted against the grant for the year
options.C: A token amount which is forfeited when the Demands for Grants for the whole year are voted
options.D: Not in addition to the grant for the whole year — it forms part of, and is adjusted against, the total grant voted for the year

e: A Vote on Account is not additional to the annual grant. It forms part of, and is adjusted against, the total grant voted for the whole year.

q: A work is executed and expenditure is incurred on it without obtaining the sanction of the authority competent to sanction the work. The expenditure so incurred is termed:

options.A: Charged expenditure
options.B: Unsanctioned expenditure, which requires to be regularised under the sanction of the competent authority
options.C: A transfer without financial effect
options.D: Expenditure on a new instrument of service

e: Expenditure incurred without sanction of the competent authority is unsanctioned expenditure. It must be regularised under the sanction of that competent authority.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stores received into the stock of a stores depot are debited to the head 'Stores Suspense'.
2. Stores issued from the stock of a depot to a work are credited to the head 'Stores Suspense'.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Stores received into depot stock are debited to Stores Suspense, and stores issued from stock to a work are credited to Stores Suspense.

q: The debit balance under 'Stores Suspense', representing the value of the stores held in stock in the depots, forms part of:

options.A: The Block Account of the Railways, on the assets side of the Balance Sheet
options.B: The Railway Pension Fund, on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet
options.C: The working expenses of the year in which the stores were received
options.D: The Traffic Suspense account of the railway

e: The Stores Suspense debit balance is the value of stores held in depots, an asset of the Railways. It forms part of the Block Account on the assets side of the Balance Sheet.

q: The Debt Head Report rendered by a zonal railway, showing the balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads, is prepared from:

options.A: The Station Balance Sheets rendered by the stations
options.B: The Pink Book maintained in the Railway Board
options.C: The Asset Registers maintained by the executive departments
options.D: The balances appearing in the General Books (Ledger) of the railway

e: The Debt Head Report is prepared from the balances under debt, suspense and remittance heads as appearing in the General Books or Ledger of the railway.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The March (Final) Account Current of a zonal railway is rendered before its March (Preliminary) Account Current.
2. The March (Final) Account Current brings into the accounts of the year the remaining adjustments which could not be included in the March (Preliminary) Account Current.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct. March Preliminary is rendered before March Final, and March Final brings in the remaining adjustments that could not be included in the Preliminary account.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes grants made under Article 275 of the Constitution from grants made under Article 282?

options.A: Grants under Article 275 are voted by the Lok Sabha every year, whereas grants under Article 282 are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Both Article 275 and Article 282 relate only to grants made by a State to the Union
options.C: Grants-in-aid under Article 275 are made by law by Parliament to States in need of assistance and are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas under Article 282 the Union or a State may make grants for any public purpose, even outside its legislative competence
options.D: Grants under Article 282 can be made only for purposes within the legislative competence of the granting Government

e: Article 275 grants-in-aid are made by law to States in need of assistance and are charged on the Consolidated Fund. Article 282 permits the Union or a State to grant for any public purpose, even outside its legislative competence.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Macro-Economic Framework Statement from the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement laid before Parliament under the FRBM Act?

options.A: The Macro-Economic Framework Statement sets out an assessment of the growth prospects of the economy and the fiscal balance of the Government, whereas the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement sets out the strategic priorities of the Government for the ensuing financial year in the fiscal area
options.B: The Macro-Economic Framework Statement lists the works included in the Pink Book, whereas the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement shows the suspense balances of the Railways
options.C: Both the statements are voted by the Lok Sabha along with the Demands for Grants
options.D: The Macro-Economic Framework Statement is prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India, whereas the Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement is prepared by the Railway Board

e: The Macro-Economic Framework Statement assesses growth prospects and fiscal balance. The Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement sets out the Government strategic fiscal priorities for the ensuing year, both under the FRBM Act.

q: The audit conducted on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India to verify that the moneys shown in the accounts as having been disbursed were legally available for, and were applied to, the services and purposes for which the grants and appropriations were made by Parliament is known as:

options.A: Performance audit
options.B: Internal audit
options.C: Stock audit
options.D: Appropriation audit

e: Checking that disbursed moneys were legally available for and applied to the purposes for which grants and appropriations were made is appropriation audit, conducted for the CAG.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The members of the Public Accounts Committee are elected by the two Houses of Parliament by the principle of proportional representation through the single transferable vote.
2. The members of the Estimates Committee are elected by the Lok Sabha from among its own members.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Public Accounts Committee members are elected by both Houses by proportional representation through the single transferable vote, and Estimates Committee members are elected by the Lok Sabha from its own members.

q: A Minister of the Union Government is proposed for membership of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament. The correct position is that:

options.A: A Minister can be a member of the Committee, and can also be its Chairman
options.B: A Minister is not eligible to be a member of the Public Accounts Committee
options.C: A Minister can be a member of the Committee but cannot attend its sittings
options.D: A Minister becomes a member of the Committee automatically on assuming office

e: A Minister is not eligible to be a member of the Public Accounts Committee. This keeps the financial committee independent of the executive it examines.

q: In examining the estimates of a Ministry, the Estimates Committee of Parliament does NOT go into:

options.A: Questions of policy underlying the estimates, the Committee confining itself to economies, improvements in organisation and efficiency consistent with the policy underlying the estimates
options.B: The estimates of any Ministry selected by it for examination
options.C: The form in which the estimates are presented to Parliament
options.D: The efficiency with which the moneys provided in the estimates are spent

e: The Estimates Committee does not examine questions of policy underlying the estimates. It confines itself to economies, organisational improvement and efficiency consistent with that policy.

q: The Railway Convention Committee of Parliament is correctly described as:

options.A: A standing committee elected every year in the same manner as the Public Accounts Committee
options.B: A committee of the Rajya Sabha alone, constituted to examine the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways
options.C: A committee which votes the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Railways
options.D: An ad hoc Parliamentary committee, constituted periodically, which reviews the financial relationship between the Railways and General Finances, including the dividend payable by the Railways

e: The Railway Convention Committee is an ad hoc Parliamentary committee constituted periodically. It reviews the financial relationship between Railways and General Finances, including the dividend payable by the Railways.

q: The presentation of the Union Budget was advanced to 1 February, with effect from the Budget for 2017-18, primarily in order to:

options.A: Enable the Economic Survey to be prepared after the close of the financial year
options.B: Enable the Supplementary Demands for Grants to be dispensed with altogether
options.C: Synchronise the financial year of the Railways with the calendar year
options.D: Complete the entire budgetary process — voting of the Demands, passing of the Appropriation Act and the Finance Act — before the commencement of the financial year, so that the authorisation for expenditure is available from 1 April itself

e: Advancing the Budget to 1 February from 2017-18 allows voting of Demands and passing of the Appropriation Act and Finance Act before the year begins, so expenditure authorisation is available from 1 April.

q: The cash balance of a zonal railway held as 'Deposits with Reserve Bank':

options.A: Is a separate balance of that railway alone, which it can draw upon independently of the Government of India
options.B: Forms part of the overall cash balance of the Government of India with the Reserve Bank of India, the zonal railway maintaining no separate ways and means position of its own
options.C: Is held by the accredited bank in a separate account for each zonal railway, outside the Government account
options.D: Represents the loans raised by that zonal railway from the Reserve Bank of India

e: Deposits with Reserve Bank is not a separate drawable balance of the zonal railway. It forms part of the overall cash balance of the Government of India with the Reserve Bank, the railway having no separate ways and means position.

q: At a monthly reconciliation, a draft statement shows the balance under the head 'Deposits with Reserve Bank' as a credit balance. This is necessarily an error, because the head:

options.A: Is closed at the end of every month and can show no balance at all
options.B: Can show a credit balance whenever the earnings of the month fall short of the payments
options.C: Invariably carries a debit balance, representing the cash balance of the Railways held with the Reserve Bank, which is an asset of the Railways
options.D: Shows a credit balance in the books of the Railway Board and a debit balance in the books of a zonal railway

e: Deposits with Reserve Bank represents cash held with the Reserve Bank, an asset, so it invariably carries a debit balance. A credit balance in a draft statement is therefore necessarily an error.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Supplementary estimates for expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India are presented to the Lok Sabha along with the Supplementary Demands for Grants.
2. Such charged supplementary estimates are submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha in the same manner as the voted Supplementary Demands.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct. Supplementary estimates for charged expenditure are presented along with Supplementary Demands, but charged expenditure is not submitted to the vote of the Lok Sabha.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Finance Commission is a constitutional body, constituted by the President under Article 280 of the Constitution.
2. The recommendations of the Finance Commission are binding on the Government of India and must be implemented without any modification.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct. The Finance Commission is a constitutional body under Article 280, but its recommendations are advisory and not binding on the Government.

q: Before the transactions of a railway are compiled into its General Books, they are first recorded in detail in the subsidiary books. In accounting terminology, such books of first record are known as the books of:

options.A: Final entry
options.B: Appropriation
options.C: Suspense entry
options.D: Original entry

e: Books in which transactions are first recorded in detail, before compilation into the General Books, are books of original entry, such as the subsidiary books.

q: The separation of railway finances from the general finances of the Government of India in 1924 was brought about, not by an Act of the Legislature, but through:

options.A: An executive order of the Governor General in Council
options.B: A resolution adopted by the Central Legislative Assembly, embodying the Separation Convention
options.C: An order of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The recommendations of the Railway Convention Committee

e: Separation of railway finances in 1924 was effected through a resolution of the Central Legislative Assembly embodying the Separation Convention, not by an Act of the Legislature.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes Article 283 of the Constitution from Article 284?

options.A: Article 283 relates to the levy of taxes, whereas Article 284 relates to the borrowing power of the Union
options.B: Both Article 283 and Article 284 relate to the constitution of the Finance Commission
options.C: Article 283 provides that the custody of the Consolidated Fund and the Contingency Fund, and payments into and withdrawals from them, shall be regulated by law made by Parliament, whereas Article 284 requires moneys received by Government officers in their official capacity, otherwise than as revenues or public moneys, to be paid into the Public Account of India
options.D: Article 284 regulates the custody of the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas Article 283 deals with moneys received by Government officers in their official capacity

e: Article 283 regulates custody of the Consolidated and Contingency Funds and payments into and withdrawals from them by law of Parliament. Article 284 requires moneys received by Government officers in official capacity, other than revenues or public moneys, to be paid into the Public Account.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the authorisation of the railway grants before the merger of the Railway Budget from the position after the merger?

options.A: Before the merger, the railway grants were authorised through the Appropriation Act of the Union Budget, and after the merger they are authorised through a separate Appropriation (Railways) Act
options.B: Both before and after the merger, the railway grants are authorised by a resolution of the Railway Board
options.C: Before the merger, the grants voted for the Railways were authorised to be withdrawn from the Consolidated Fund of India through a separate Appropriation (Railways) Act, whereas after the merger they are authorised through the Appropriation Act passed on the Demands for Grants of the Union Budget
options.D: After the merger, no Appropriation Act is required for the expenditure of the Railways

e: Before merger, railway grants were authorised through a separate Appropriation (Railways) Act. After merger they are authorised through the Appropriation Act passed on the Union Budget Demands for Grants.

q: After the Finance Commission has submitted its recommendations to the President, the Government lays them before each House of Parliament along with:

options.A: A Supplementary Demand for Grant giving effect to the recommendations
options.B: The report of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India on the recommendations
options.C: A resolution seeking the approval of both Houses for each recommendation
options.D: An explanatory memorandum as to the action taken on the recommendations

e: Under Article 281, Finance Commission recommendations are laid before each House of Parliament together with an explanatory memorandum as to the action taken on them.

q: The administrative expenses of the Election Commission of India are not submitted to the annual vote of the Lok Sabha, because they are:

options.A: Met out of the Public Account of India, which requires no authorisation
options.B: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Borne by the State Governments in proportion to their electorates
options.D: Provided for in the Contingency Fund of India

e: The administrative expenses of the Election Commission are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 324(6) read with Article 112(3). Charged expenditure is not submitted to the vote of Parliament, though it can be discussed.

q: The estimates of the receipts of the Government, as presented in the Annual Financial Statement:

options.A: Are not submitted to the vote of Parliament, the voting of Parliament being confined to the Demands for Grants for expenditure
options.B: Are voted by the Lok Sabha in the same manner as the Demands for Grants
options.C: Are voted only by the Rajya Sabha
options.D: Require a separate Appropriation Act for the receipts of the year

e: Under Article 113, only expenditure is presented as Demands for Grants and voted by the Lok Sabha. The estimates of receipts in the Annual Financial Statement under Article 112 are shown for information and are not put to vote.

q: Although the Finance Bill is introduced in the Lok Sabha immediately after the presentation of the Budget, its consideration and passing are taken up only at the stage when:

options.A: The Demands for Grants have been voted and the Appropriation Bill has been passed
options.B: The general discussion on the Budget is about to commence
options.C: The Budget has just been presented, on the same day
options.D: The Appropriation Accounts of the previous year have been laid before Parliament

e: The Finance Bill, which gives effect to the taxation proposals, is taken up for consideration and passing only after the Demands for Grants are voted and the Appropriation Bill is passed, completing the expenditure authorisation first.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. No discussion on the Budget takes place in Parliament on the day on which it is presented.
2. During the general discussion on the Budget which follows its presentation, no motion can be moved and no voting on the Demands for Grants takes place.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: By convention no discussion takes place on the day the Budget is presented. During the general discussion that follows, only the broad policy and figures are discussed; no motion is moved and no Demand is voted at that stage.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The recovery of the principal of a loan advanced by the Government is treated as a revenue receipt of the Government.
2. Interest received by the Government on the loans and advances made by it is a non-tax revenue receipt.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Recovery of loan principal is a capital receipt as it reduces an asset, so statement 1 is wrong. Interest on loans and advances is a non-tax revenue receipt, so statement 2 is correct.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Revenue receipts of the Government neither create a liability for the Government nor lead to a reduction in its assets.
2. Capital receipts of the Government never create any liability for repayment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Revenue receipts neither create a liability nor reduce assets, so statement 1 is correct. Capital receipts can create liability, for example market borrowings, so statement 2 saying they never create liability is wrong.

q: The apportionment of goods earnings among the railways over which the traffic has passed is dealt with in the Traffic Book in:

options.A: Part A, along with the coaching earnings
options.B: Neither part, goods earnings being never apportioned
options.C: Part B
options.D: A separate part maintained only for goods traffic

e: In the Traffic Book, Part A deals with coaching earnings and Part B deals with goods earnings, including the apportionment of goods earnings among the railways over which the traffic passed.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Transfer transactions originating in the books of a unit are 'outward transfers' for that unit.
2. The same transactions are 'inward transfers' for the respondent unit which receives the transfer advice.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A transfer originating in a unit is an outward transfer for that unit, and the same transaction is an inward transfer for the respondent unit receiving the transfer advice. Both statements correctly describe transfer transactions.

q: A proposal involving expenditure on a 'New Service', not contemplated in the approved budget, is examined for the approval of Parliament with reference to the provisions of the Indian Railway Finance Code contained in para:
e: Para 370 of the Indian Railway Finance Code Volume I deals with expenditure on a New Service not contemplated in the approved budget and the procedure for obtaining the approval of Parliament for it.

q: The Railways maintain certain lines for strategic (defence) considerations, on which the working results show a loss. Such working losses of the Strategic Lines are:

options.A: Borne by the zonal railway concerned out of its own earnings in all cases
options.B: Borne by General Finances, by way of subsidy in respect of the strategic lines
options.C: Debited to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways
options.D: Written off against the Capital Fund of the Railways

e: Lines maintained purely for strategic or defence reasons are unremunerative by policy, so their working losses are borne by General Finances by way of subsidy to the Railways for strategic lines.

q: Government accounts are divided into three parts — Part I (Consolidated Fund), Part II and Part III (Public Account). The Contingency Fund of India finds its place in:

options.A: Part II of the Government accounts
options.B: Part I, as a section of the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Part III, along with the Public Account of India
options.D: The accounts of the Reserve Bank of India, and not in the Government accounts

e: Government accounts are kept in three parts under Article 266: Part I is the Consolidated Fund, Part II is the Contingency Fund of India, and Part III is the Public Account. Hence the Contingency Fund is in Part II.

q: The accounts of a division of a zonal railway are correctly described as follows:

options.A: The division is an independent accounting unit rendering its own monthly Account Current to the Railway Board
options.B: The division renders its accounts directly to the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The division maintains its own General Books and Balance Sheet, independent of the zonal headquarters
options.D: The division is not a separate accounting unit — its transactions are incorporated in the accounts compiled at the headquarters of the zonal railway

e: A division is not a separate accounting unit. Its transactions are incorporated in the accounts compiled at zonal railway headquarters, which alone renders the monthly Account Current.

q: The head of the Accounts Department of a zonal railway, who also functions as the financial adviser to the General Manager of the railway, is the:

options.A: Principal Director of Audit
options.B: Controller General of Accounts
options.C: Principal Financial Adviser
options.D: Financial Commissioner (Railways)

e: The Principal Financial Adviser heads the Accounts Department of a zonal railway and functions as financial adviser to the General Manager. The Financial Commissioner (Railways) holds that role at the Railway Board level.

q: Treasury Bills, through which the Government of India raises short-term funds, are issued in maturities of:

options.A: 30 days, 60 days and 90 days
options.B: 91 days, 182 days and 364 days
options.C: One year, two years and five years
options.D: 14 days, 28 days and 56 days

e: Treasury Bills are short-term instruments issued by the Government of India through the Reserve Bank in the standard maturities of 91 days, 182 days and 364 days, at a discount and redeemed at par.

q: An existing asset is renewed by a materially better and heavier asset, so that its capacity and value stand materially enhanced. The cost of the renewal is apportioned as under:

options.A: The entire cost is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: The entire cost is charged to Capital in all cases
options.C: The entire cost is charged to the ordinary working expenses of the year
options.D: The cost of replacing the original asset, on a like-for-like basis, is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, and the additional cost attributable to the betterment and enhancement is charged to Capital or the Development Fund

e: On betterment renewal, the like-for-like replacement cost is charged to the Depreciation Reserve Fund, which finances renewals, and only the additional cost of the improvement and enhanced capacity is charged to Capital or Development Fund.

q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India holds office for a term of:

options.A: Five years from the date of assumption of office, or until he attains the age of sixty-two years, whichever is earlier
options.B: Six years from the date of assumption of office, or until he attains the age of sixty-five years, whichever is earlier
options.C: Six years from the date of assumption of office, with no limit of age
options.D: Until he attains the age of sixty-two years, there being no fixed term of years

e: Under the CAG (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971, the Comptroller and Auditor General holds office for six years or until attaining 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.

q: Before entering upon his office, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India makes and subscribes an oath or affirmation before:

options.A: The Chief Justice of India
options.B: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.C: The Prime Minister
options.D: The President, or some person appointed in that behalf by the President

e: Under Article 148(2), before entering office the CAG makes and subscribes an oath or affirmation before the President, or a person appointed by the President for that purpose, as per the Third Schedule.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The salary and other conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India are determined by Parliament by law.
2. The conditions of service of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India cannot be varied to his disadvantage after his appointment.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Article 148(3) provides that the salary and conditions of service of the CAG are determined by Parliament by law, and Article 148(4) bars variation of his conditions of service to his disadvantage after appointment.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Commission:
1. The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members, appointed by the President.
2. The members of the Finance Commission are elected by the two Houses of Parliament by proportional representation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under Article 280(2), the Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President. Statement 2 is wrong as members are appointed, not elected by Parliament.

q: Under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951, the Chairman of the Finance Commission is to be selected from among persons who have:

options.A: Been Judges of a High Court, or are qualified to be appointed as such Judges
options.B: Special knowledge of economics
options.C: Experience in public affairs
options.D: Served as the Finance Secretary to the Government of India

e: Under the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1951, the Chairman is selected from among persons having experience in public affairs; the other qualifications listed apply to the other members.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 292 of the Constitution, the executive power of the Union extends to borrowing upon the security of the Consolidated Fund of India within such limits, if any, as may be fixed by Parliament by law.
2. No borrowing can be undertaken by the Government of India without the prior approval of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Article 292 empowers the Union to borrow on the security of the Consolidated Fund of India within limits fixed by Parliament by law, so statement 1 is correct. No CAG approval is needed for borrowing, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: The members of the Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways are:

options.A: Elected by the Lok Sabha from among its own members
options.B: Nominated by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha from among the members of their respective Houses
options.C: Appointed by the President on the advice of the Council of Ministers
options.D: Ex-officio members, being the Chairmen of the other Parliamentary committees

e: Members of the Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways, 21 from Lok Sabha and 10 from Rajya Sabha, are nominated by the Speaker and the Chairman of Rajya Sabha respectively from among members of their Houses.

q: The statutory auditors of a Government company, such as a railway public sector undertaking, are appointed by:

options.A: The Board of Directors of the company
options.B: The shareholders of the company in its annual general meeting
options.C: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Ministry of Railways, as the administrative Ministry

e: Under Section 139(5) of the Companies Act 2013, the statutory auditors of a Government company are appointed by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement from the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement laid before Parliament under the FRBM Act?

options.A: Both the statements set out three-year rolling targets for the fiscal deficit alone
options.B: The Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement sets out the expenditure projections of the Ministries, whereas the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement sets out the targets for fiscal indicators
options.C: Both the statements are voted by Parliament along with the Demands for Grants
options.D: The Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement sets out three-year rolling targets for specified fiscal indicators, whereas the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement sets out the expenditure projections of the Ministries for three years

e: Under the FRBM Act, the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement lays down three-year rolling targets for specified fiscal indicators, while the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement gives three-year expenditure projections of Ministries.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Budget document 'Budget at a Glance' from the 'Key to Budget Documents'?

options.A: 'Budget at a Glance' presents a brief summary of the Budget, showing the receipts, expenditure and deficit indicators in a nutshell, whereas the 'Key to Budget Documents' explains the various Budget documents and the terms used in them
options.B: 'Budget at a Glance' explains the various Budget documents, whereas the 'Key to Budget Documents' presents the summary figures of the Budget
options.C: Both the documents contain the detailed Demands for Grants of the Ministries
options.D: 'Budget at a Glance' is presented only to the Rajya Sabha, whereas the 'Key to Budget Documents' is presented only to the Lok Sabha

e: Budget at a Glance is a nutshell summary showing receipts, expenditure and deficit indicators. The Key to Budget Documents is a guide that explains the various Budget documents and the terms used in them.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Pink Book' of the Railways from the 'Detailed Demands for Grants' of the Ministry of Railways?

options.A: The Pink Book gives the head-wise break-up of the revenue estimates, whereas the Detailed Demands for Grants list the works included in the Works Programme
options.B: Both the documents list only the works included in the Works Programme, Plan Head-wise
options.C: The Pink Book lists the works included in the Works Programme, arranged Plan Head-wise with the provision made for them, whereas the Detailed Demands for Grants give the detailed head-wise break-up of the estimates included in the Demand for Grants
options.D: The Pink Book is a document of the Ministry of Finance, whereas the Detailed Demands for Grants are prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: The Pink Book is the Works Programme book listing sanctioned works Plan Head-wise with the provision made for each. The Detailed Demands for Grants give the detailed head-wise break-up of the estimates in the Demand.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Budget document 'Receipts Budget' from the 'Expenditure Profile'?

options.A: The Receipts Budget presents the pattern of expenditure ministry-wise, whereas the Expenditure Profile analyses the tax revenues of the Government
options.B: The Receipts Budget presents a detailed analysis of the tax revenues, non-tax revenues and capital receipts of the Government, whereas the Expenditure Profile presents a broad snapshot of the pattern of the total expenditure of the Government, ministry-wise and scheme-wise
options.C: Both the documents explain the provisions of the Finance Bill clause by clause
options.D: The Receipts Budget is laid only before the Rajya Sabha, whereas the Expenditure Profile is laid only before the Lok Sabha

e: The Receipts Budget analyses tax revenue, non-tax revenue and capital receipts in detail. The Expenditure Profile gives a broad snapshot of total expenditure, ministry-wise and scheme-wise.

q:
Consider the following statements about an error of original entry:
1. Where a transaction is first recorded in the book of original entry with a wrong amount, the same wrong amount being both debited and credited, the agreement of the Trial Balance is not disturbed.
2. An error of original entry is necessarily disclosed by the disagreement of the Trial Balance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: An error of original entry with a wrong amount debited and credited equally does not disturb Trial Balance agreement, so statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is wrong as such an error is not disclosed by the Trial Balance.

q:
Consider the following statements about the complete reversal of an entry in the books:
1. Where an entry is completely reversed, the account which should have been debited being credited and the account which should have been credited being debited, the Trial Balance necessarily disagrees.
2. Notwithstanding such a complete reversal, the total debits in the books remain equal to the total credits, and the Trial Balance still agrees.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In a complete reversal the wrong debit and wrong credit are of equal amount, so total debits still equal total credits and the Trial Balance agrees. Statement 2 is correct and statement 1 is wrong.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Transfer Certificate' from a 'Transfer Entry Order' in railway accounts?

options.A: Both the documents are used only for recording cash receipts at stations
options.B: A Transfer Certificate authorises a journal adjustment within the books of one unit, whereas a Transfer Entry Order intimates a debit raised by one railway against another
options.C: A Transfer Certificate is issued by the Reserve Bank of India, whereas a Transfer Entry Order is issued by the Cash & Pay Office
options.D: A Transfer Certificate is the advice by which one railway intimates a transfer debit or credit raised against another railway, whereas a Transfer Entry Order is the document which authorises a journal (transfer) adjustment within the books of the accounting unit itself

e: A Transfer Certificate is the advice by which one railway intimates a transfer debit or credit raised against another railway. A Transfer Entry Order authorises a journal adjustment within the books of the same accounting unit.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Debt Head Report' from the 'Trial Balance' of a railway?

options.A: The Debt Head Report tests the arithmetical accuracy of the General Books, whereas the Trial Balance shows the balances under the debt heads
options.B: The Debt Head Report exhibits the balances outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads of account, whereas the Trial Balance is the list of the balances extracted from the General Books to test the arithmetical accuracy of the accounts
options.C: Both the statements are rendered only at the close of the financial year
options.D: The Debt Head Report is prepared by the Audit Department, whereas the Trial Balance is prepared by the Railway Board

e: The Debt Head Report shows balances outstanding under debt, suspense and remittance heads. The Trial Balance is the list of balances extracted from the General Books to test arithmetical accuracy of the accounts.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'initial records' from 'subsidiary records' in the railway accounting system?

options.A: Initial records are maintained in the Accounts Office, whereas subsidiary records are maintained at stations
options.B: Both initial records and subsidiary records are General Books of the railway
options.C: Initial records are the primary records prepared in the executive offices and at stations, such as measurement books, muster rolls and station returns, which form the basis of the accounts, whereas subsidiary records are the registers maintained in the Accounts Office, such as the Works Registers and Suspense Registers, in support of the compilation of the accounts
options.D: Initial records are prepared by the Audit Department, whereas subsidiary records are prepared by the Railway Board

e: Initial records are primary records made in executive offices and at stations, like measurement books, muster rolls and station returns. Subsidiary records are registers kept in the Accounts Office, like Works and Suspense Registers, supporting compilation.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the recoupment of an advance taken from the Contingency Fund of India?

options.A: Advance taken from the Contingency Fund to meet urgent unforeseen expenditure — Supplementary Demands presented to Parliament — Supplementary Grant voted and Appropriation Act passed — Contingency Fund recouped
options.B: Supplementary Grant voted — Contingency Fund recouped — advance taken from the Contingency Fund — Supplementary Demands presented
options.C: Contingency Fund recouped — advance taken from the Contingency Fund — Appropriation Act passed — Supplementary Demands presented
options.D: Advance taken from the Contingency Fund — Contingency Fund recouped out of the balances of the Railway Funds — Supplementary Demands presented — Appropriation Act passed

e: The correct order is: advance from the Contingency Fund for urgent unforeseen expenditure, then Supplementary Demands are presented, the grant is voted and the Appropriation Act passed, and only then the Fund is recouped.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the regularisation of expenditure incurred in excess of a grant?

options.A: Demand for Excess Grant presented — excess expenditure incurred — examination by the Public Accounts Committee — reflection in the Appropriation Accounts
options.B: Examination by the Public Accounts Committee — excess expenditure incurred — Demand for Excess Grant presented — reflection in the Appropriation Accounts
options.C: Excess expenditure incurred — Demand for Excess Grant presented and voted at once — reflection in the Appropriation Accounts — examination by the Public Accounts Committee
options.D: Excess expenditure incurred — excess reflected in the Appropriation Accounts of the year — excess examined by the Public Accounts Committee — Demand for Excess Grant presented to and voted by the Lok Sabha — authorisation through the Appropriation Act

e: Excess is first incurred, then reflected in the Appropriation Accounts, then examined by the Public Accounts Committee, and finally regularised by a Demand for Excess Grant voted by the Lok Sabha and authorised by Appropriation Act.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the finalisation of the Works Programme of a zonal railway and the control of expenditure on the works included in it?

options.A: Final Works Programme finalised — Preliminary Works Programme proposals submitted — budget allotment communicated — detailed estimates sanctioned
options.B: Preliminary Works Programme proposals submitted by the zonal railway — Budget approved and budget allotment communicated by the Railway Board — Final Works Programme finalised — detailed estimates sanctioned by the competent authority — expenditure watched work-wise through the Works Register
options.C: Detailed estimates sanctioned — Preliminary Works Programme proposals submitted — expenditure watched through the Works Register — Final Works Programme finalised
options.D: Budget allotment communicated — detailed estimates sanctioned — Preliminary Works Programme proposals submitted — Final Works Programme finalised

e: The sequence is: Preliminary Works Programme proposals from the zonal railway, Budget approval and allotment communicated by the Railway Board, Final Works Programme finalised, detailed estimates sanctioned, and expenditure watched work-wise in the Works Register.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in obtaining a Supplementary Grant during a financial year?

options.A: Supplementary Demands voted — need for additional funds arises — authorisation through the Appropriation Act — Final Grant enhanced
options.B: Need for additional funds arises — authorisation through the Appropriation Act — Supplementary Demands presented — Final Grant enhanced
options.C: Need for additional funds, or for expenditure on a new service, arises during the year — Supplementary Demands presented to the Lok Sabha — Demands voted by the Lok Sabha — authorisation through the Appropriation Act — Final Grant for the year stands enhanced
options.D: Final Grant enhanced by re-appropriation — Supplementary Demands presented — Demands voted — authorisation through the Appropriation Act

e: When need for additional funds or a new service arises, Supplementary Demands are presented to the Lok Sabha, voted by it, and authorised through the Appropriation Act, whereby the Final Grant for the year stands enhanced.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the apportionment of through-traffic earnings among the zonal railways?

options.A: The full earnings of through traffic are brought to account by the originating railway — the station balance sheets and returns are received in the Traffic Accounts Office — apportionment is made in the Traffic Book in proportion to the distance traversed over each railway — the net result of apportionment is adjusted through transfer transactions
options.B: Apportionment is made in the Traffic Book — the full earnings are brought to account by the originating railway — the net result is adjusted in cash — the station returns are received
options.C: The net result of apportionment is adjusted through transfer transactions — apportionment is made in the Traffic Book — the station returns are received — the earnings are brought to account
options.D: The station returns are received — the net result is remitted in cash to each railway — apportionment is made in the Traffic Book — the earnings are brought to account by the Railway Board

e: The originating railway first brings the full through-traffic earnings to account on receipt of station returns, apportionment is then made in the Traffic Book by distance over each railway, and the net result is adjusted through transfer transactions.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an 'Excess Grant' from a 'Vote of Credit'?

options.A: Both an Excess Grant and a Vote of Credit are taken in advance, before any expenditure is incurred
options.B: An Excess Grant is voted after the close of the year to regularise expenditure already incurred in excess of a grant, whereas a Vote of Credit is an advance grant for a service which, on account of its magnitude or indefinite character, cannot be stated with the details ordinarily given in a Demand for Grant
options.C: An Excess Grant is voted by the Rajya Sabha, whereas a Vote of Credit is voted by the Lok Sabha
options.D: An Excess Grant forms part of the services of the current year, whereas a Vote of Credit regularises the excess expenditure of a past year

e: An Excess Grant is voted after the year closes to regularise expenditure already incurred beyond a grant. A Vote of Credit is an advance grant for a service too large or indefinite to be detailed in a normal Demand.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an advance from the Contingency Fund of India from a 'Vote of Credit'?

options.A: An advance from the Contingency Fund is itself a grant voted by Parliament, whereas a Vote of Credit is recouped to a fund after authorisation
options.B: Both an advance from the Contingency Fund and a Vote of Credit are drawn from a standing fund at the disposal of the President
options.C: A Vote of Credit is taken to meet expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament, whereas an advance from the Contingency Fund is a grant voted by the Lok Sabha
options.D: An advance from the Contingency Fund is drawn from a standing fund placed at the disposal of the President to meet urgent unforeseen expenditure pending authorisation by Parliament, and is recouped after such authorisation, whereas a Vote of Credit is itself a grant voted by the Lok Sabha for a service of a magnitude or indefinite character

e: A Contingency Fund advance is drawn from the standing imprest at the disposal of the President pending Parliament authorisation and is later recouped. A Vote of Credit is itself a grant voted by the Lok Sabha for an indefinite service.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'token provision' in the Works Programme from a 'token grant'?

options.A: A token provision is a nominal grant voted by Parliament for a new service, whereas a token grant is a nominal provision made in the Pink Book for an unsanctioned work
options.B: Both a token provision and a token grant are grants voted by the Lok Sabha for new services
options.C: A token provision dispenses with the sanction of the work, whereas a token grant dispenses with the approval of Parliament for a new service
options.D: A token provision is the nominal provision made in the budget for a work included in the Works Programme but not yet sanctioned by the competent authority, whereas a token grant is the nominal grant taken from Parliament for a new service whose cost can be met by re-appropriation within the grant

e: A token provision is a nominal budget provision in the Pink Book for a work included in the Works Programme but not yet sanctioned. A token grant is a nominal grant from Parliament for a new service whose cost is met by re-appropriation.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Demands Payable' from 'Unpaid Wages' in railway accounts?

options.A: Both the heads represent wages drawn but remaining undisbursed to staff
options.B: 'Demands Payable' represents advances made to staff, whereas 'Unpaid Wages' represents amounts due to outside parties for goods received
options.C: 'Demands Payable' represents amounts due by the Railways to outside parties for goods and services received, pending payment, whereas 'Unpaid Wages' represents wages and salaries drawn but remaining undisbursed to the staff entitled to them
options.D: 'Demands Payable' is a remittance head, whereas 'Unpaid Wages' is an earnings head

e: Demands Payable are amounts due to outside parties for goods and services received, pending payment. Unpaid Wages are wages and salaries drawn but remaining undisbursed to the staff entitled to them.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an 'imprest' from 'Miscellaneous Advances' in railway accounts?

options.A: An imprest is an amount due from an outside party for services rendered, whereas Miscellaneous Advances are a standing advance for petty expenditure
options.B: An imprest is a fixed standing advance given to an officer to meet petty and contingent expenditure, which is recouped when he renders an account of the expenditure incurred out of it, whereas Miscellaneous Advances are advances made by the Railways which are held under a suspense head pending recovery or adjustment in due course
options.C: Both an imprest and Miscellaneous Advances represent deposits received from contractors
options.D: An imprest is operated only by the Cash & Pay Office, whereas Miscellaneous Advances are operated only by stations

e: An imprest is a fixed standing advance to an officer for petty contingent expenditure, recouped on rendering account. Miscellaneous Advances are advances held under a suspense head pending recovery or adjustment in due course.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Capital-at-charge' from the 'Capital Fund' of the Railways?

options.A: The two expressions mean the same thing, both representing the total capital invested in the Railways
options.B: Capital-at-charge is a fund fed by appropriations from the surplus, whereas the Capital Fund is shown on the assets side of the Balance Sheet
options.C: Capital-at-charge represents only the assets financed from the Capital Fund
options.D: Capital-at-charge is the total capital invested in the Railways, shown on the liabilities side of its Balance Sheet, whereas the Capital Fund is a fund maintained in the Public Account, fed by appropriations from the surplus (net revenue), for financing capital works out of the Railways' internal resources

e: Capital-at-charge is the total capital invested in the Railways, shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet. The Capital Fund is a Public Account fund fed from surplus and used to finance capital works from internal resources.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'gross earnings' of the Railways from their 'net revenue' for a year?

options.A: The gross earnings of the Railways are the total earnings of the year — coaching, goods and sundry other earnings — whereas the net revenue (surplus) is the amount remaining after deducting from the gross earnings the total working expenses, including the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund
options.B: The gross earnings are arrived at after deducting the working expenses, whereas the net revenue is the total of the coaching and goods earnings
options.C: Both the gross earnings and the net revenue represent the total earnings before meeting the working expenses
options.D: The net revenue includes the Gross Budgetary Support received during the year, whereas the gross earnings do not include the traffic earnings

e: Gross earnings are total coaching, goods and sundry earnings of the year. Net revenue or surplus is what remains after deducting total working expenses, including appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and Pension Fund, from gross earnings.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'transfer transactions' from 'remittance transactions' in railway accounts?

options.A: Both transfer transactions and remittance transactions involve an actual movement of cash between the railways concerned
options.B: Transfer transactions record moneys in the course of settlement between accounting circles, whereas remittance transactions are book adjustments between accounting units
options.C: Transfer transactions are book adjustments between accounting units in respect of receipts and expenditure effected by one unit on behalf of another, without movement of cash, whereas remittance transactions record moneys remitted from one accounting circle to another which are in the course of settlement, pending final adjustment
options.D: Transfer transactions are confined to transactions with the Reserve Bank of India, whereas remittance transactions are confined to transactions between stations

e: Transfer transactions are book adjustments between accounting units for receipts and expenditure effected by one unit for another, with no cash movement. Remittance transactions record moneys in transit between accounting circles pending settlement.

q: Receipts from retiring rooms provided at railway stations for the use of passengers are classified in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Passenger earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Sundry Other Earnings
options.D: Other Coaching Earnings

e: Receipts from retiring rooms at stations are not passenger, goods or other coaching earnings. They are classified under Sundry Other Earnings in the railway earnings classification.

q: Resources raised by the Indian Railway Finance Corporation through the issue of bonds in the capital market and made available to the Railways for the acquisition of rolling stock form part, in the financing of the Railways' annual plan outlay, of:

options.A: Gross Budgetary Support
options.B: The internal resources of the Railways
options.C: Extra Budgetary Resources
options.D: Appropriations to the Capital Fund

e: Funds raised by IRFC through market bonds for acquiring rolling stock are Extra Budgetary Resources in the financing of the annual plan outlay, being neither Gross Budgetary Support nor the Railways own internal resources.

q:
Consider the following statements about a Vote on Account:
1. A Vote on Account is ordinarily passed by the Lok Sabha without the detailed discussion which the Demands for Grants undergo.
2. The amount granted through a Vote on Account forms part of the total grant for the year and is merged in it when the full grant is voted.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A Vote on Account is ordinarily passed without the detailed discussion that Demands undergo, and its amount forms part of and is merged in the total grant for the year when the full grant is voted. Both statements are correct.

q: Which of the following is NOT recorded in the Journal Book of a railway?

options.A: Opening entries, bringing in the balances of assets and liabilities at the commencement of the year
options.B: Transfer (adjustment) entries between heads of account
options.C: Closing entries, closing the revenue accounts at the end of the year
options.D: Cash receipts and payments effected through the Cash & Pay Office, which are recorded in the Main Cash Book

e: The Journal Book records opening entries, transfer or adjustment entries and closing entries. Cash receipts and payments through the Cash and Pay Office are recorded in the Main Cash Book, not the Journal Book.

q: The amount accumulated under 'Manufacturing Suspense' against a job undertaken in a railway workshop comprises:

options.A: Labour charges, material charges and on-cost charges booked to the job
options.B: Labour charges only, the material being charged directly to the final head
options.C: Only the proforma on-cost charges of the workshop
options.D: Only the cost of stores issued from the stores depot for the job

e: Manufacturing Suspense accumulates the full cost of a workshop job, comprising labour charges, material charges and on-cost charges booked to that job, pending out-turn and adjustment to the final head.
